adjudication_records.issue_text: `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:22 renders imported HTML unescaped in the forum's origin, enabling stored XSS via attacker-influenced embedded content

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a path where attacker-controlled HTML can be stored and later rendered unescaped. In TopicEmbed.import, RSS/Atom content is taken from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` as `i.content`, then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is used and the resulting string is passed to `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. Post#cook was changed so that when `cook_method == :raw_html` it returns `raw` directly, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the post body is rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output that stored HTML verbatim. Therefore malicious HTML from the feed (or other import sources) can become stored XSS on the Discourse origin when the embed page is viewed.

The `Imported from` footer in app/models/topic_embed.rb:13–21 interpolates `url` into an href attribute without escaping, allowing markup injection via a single quote in the URL

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import the code appends HTML directly to `contents` using `"#{url}"` (single-quoted href attribute) without any escaping. The only validation on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent a single quote or other characters inside the URL. If `url` contains a `'`, it can break out of the href attribute and inject arbitrary markup/JS. This risk is amplified because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing any normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Therefore the finding describes a real, verifiable injection/XSS issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The revision path in app/models/topic_embed.rb:35–42 never updates the topic title, leaving topics with stale titles indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path (`else` branch around lines 35–42) only revises the existing post’s raw HTML via `PostRevisor#revise!(user, ...)` and updates `embed.content_sha1`. It never updates the topic/post title. Additionally, `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` only (`Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`), so a title-only change won’t even trigger the update block. Therefore, imported topics can keep an outdated title indefinitely even if the remote/feed title changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 has no error handling and the job has retry: false, so transient failures kill the poll and can surface unhandled exceptions in the embed request path

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `rescue`. `open` (open-uri) can raise transient network/HTTP exceptions (e.g., SocketError, OpenURI::HTTPError, timeouts), which would crash the job. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such transient failures will not be retried and polling/import will stop for that run. Additionally, TopicRetriever calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` during retrieval, so an exception here can abort embed topic retrieval (even if not strictly in the synchronous controller request path, it will fail the retrieval workflow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded feed import loop in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30-35`: There is no cap on `rss.items` and no pagination windowing, leading to long-running Sidekiq jobs, OOM, and excessive database/transaction load for large RSS feeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item with no limit, batching, or time/windowing. This is verifiable in the diff: there is no cap on number of items processed per run, and no mechanism (e.g., using `feed_key`/Last-Modified/ETag) to avoid re-processing large feeds. Even though `TopicEmbed.import` may dedupe by `embed_url`, the Sidekiq job still must parse and iterate the entire feed each hour, which can become long-running and memory/DB intensive for large feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full feed download and parse into memory with no size limit in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27`: `open(url)` reads the entire body into memory with no `Content-Length`/max-size guard, no timeout, and follows redirects, risking OOM from large payloads.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after `require 'open-uri'`. This uses Ruby's open-uri without specifying any timeouts (`open_timeout`, `read_timeout`) or maximum download size. `SimpleRSS.parse` will consume the response body to parse the feed, so a very large response (or slow/never-ending response) can tie up the job and potentially exhaust memory. No guards against redirects or content length are present in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import_remote` reads the whole remote body into memory with no limit or timeout in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:45-46`: `open(url).read` slurps the entire page without a max-size, open timeout, or redirect cap, risking worker memory exhaustion.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the diff adds `open(url).read` and passes the full string into `Readability::Document` (lines shown around `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`). This unconditionally reads the entire remote response body into memory and does not supply any `open-uri` options (e.g., open/read timeouts, max bytes, or redirect limits). Because this runs in background jobs (`TopicRetriever`/feed import), a large/slow/malicious response can plausibly exhaust worker memory or hang the job. This is directly evidenced by the added code.

`absolutize_urls` reparses full HTML with Nokogiri on every import/update in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:67-80`: The Nokogiri parse + CSS scans scale with content size and run across all items hourly, even when only the SHA1 changed.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` does parse the content with Nokogiri and scans `a`/`img` nodes, but that work is only performed when creating a new embed or when the content SHA1 *differs* (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), not “across all items hourly” unconditionally and not when content is unchanged. Since absolutizing URLs requires parsing, this is an expected cost rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff, and the finding’s key premise (it runs even when content hasn’t changed) is not supported by the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-import transaction in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:24-37` holds row locks while running PostCreator/Revisor: Enqueuing jobs, callbacks, and table updates inside a single transaction increases lock contention and bloat during the hourly poll.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only explicit transaction is `Topic.transaction do ... end` around creating a new post/topic and the `TopicEmbed` row. The diff does not show any job enqueuing inside that transaction, and any mention of callbacks/other side effects happening within `PostCreator#create` is not verifiable from this diff. Using a transaction here is a common correctness measure (ensuring the post/topic and embed row are created atomically), and the claimed lock contention/bloat during hourly polling is a speculative performance concern rather than a clear defect introduced by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hourly poll in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25-26` has no de-duplication against in-flight runs: Overlapping runs can duplicate fetch/parse/Nokogiri/transaction costs, even though `content_sha1` prevents double-inserts.

adjudication.rationale: `Jobs::PollFeed` is scheduled hourly (`recurrence { hourly }`) and `execute` unconditionally calls `poll_feed` when settings are present. `poll_feed` performs a full `open` + `SimpleRSS.parse` and iterates all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each, but there is no lock/redis key/unique job mechanism to prevent concurrent/in-flight runs. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` can invoke `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, increasing the chance of overlap with the scheduled run. While `TopicEmbed.import` will usually avoid duplicate inserts via the `topic_embeds.embed_url` unique index and `content_sha1` change check, overlapping runs can still duplicate fetch/parse/iteration and can race on new URLs (both see `embed.blank?` before insert), causing extra work and potentially a unique-index exception on the second insert attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: imported external content rendered as raw HTML without sanitization, bypassing cooking pipeline and after_post_cook filter

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping both the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and the `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` hook. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from externally sourced content (RSS via `Jobs::PollFeed` using `i.content` and remote fetch via `open(url)`/readability) and explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. That external HTML is then rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb`, and since `post.cooked == post.raw` for these posts, arbitrary HTML from the feed/remote page can be stored and served without sanitization, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: XSS via unsanitized URL in imported-from attribution link allowing HTML attribute breakout
Breaking CLI contract: `--category` option removed from Disqus import task and `created_at` option silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither `TopicEmbed.import_remote` nor `TopicEmbed.import` pass a `created_at` into `PostCreator` (they only pass `title`, `raw`, `skip_validations`, `cook_method`). So both the `--category` CLI option and imported `created_at` behavior are removed, which is a clear, verifiable breaking behavior change for the Disqus import task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to already-applied migration `create_top_topics` risks data loss on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That introduces a clear data-loss risk if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, rollback+reapply, or a database where the table exists but the migration isn’t recorded). The risk is directly attributable to the added `force: true` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External HTTP fetches in PollFeed and TopicEmbed.import_remote have no timeout, size limit, or SSRF guard
postMessage targetOrigin in embed layout uses full referer string instead of origin, causing resize failure if referer is empty
embed.js origin check is substring-based (`indexOf`) instead of exact equality
`TopicEmbed.import` update path does not re-set `cook_method`, mangling content if it was previously changed

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path (`embed` exists and `content_sha1` differs) revises the existing `post` via `PostRevisor` but does not touch `post.cook_method`. However, the post created on the initial import is explicitly given `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and nothing in this diff shows any code that later changes `cook_method` away from `:raw_html`. Therefore, there is no verifiable bug in the diff itself: the update preserves the existing cook_method (which should already be `:raw_html` for imported posts), so “mangling content if it was previously changed” depends on an external/unspecified change not evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reloads at 30s but response cache is 60s, causing extended 'Loading...' display

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, both the normal and the `render 'loading'` path end by calling `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, which will set caching headers for 60s. The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) reloads the page after 30s. If the response is cached (browser/proxy/CDN) according to the 60s cache headers, the reload at 30s can serve the cached Loading page again, potentially delaying display of the real embedded content beyond the intended 30s refresh interval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` called synchronously inside `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` blocks Sidekiq worker

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` directly instantiates and runs `Jobs::PollFeed` via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports items, so calling it synchronously will make the current execution (e.g., the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq worker that invokes `TopicRetriever#retrieve`) spend potentially significant time polling/parsing the feed instead of just enqueueing work. This blocks that Sidekiq worker thread for the duration and also bypasses Sidekiq scheduling/options (e.g., `sidekiq_options retry: false`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via raw rendering of imported feed content in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:18 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-17

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a deliberate bypass of Discourse’s cooking/sanitization pipeline for imported content. In app/models/post.rb, `cook` now returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == :raw_html`. TopicEmbed.import passes RSS/remote HTML directly into PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) after only doing URL absolutization via Nokogiri, not sanitization. Then app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders that content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output any embedded HTML/JS from the feed/article. PollFeed pulls `i.content` from the feed and only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (no sanitization), so malicious feed content could be stored and executed when embedded/highlights are viewed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NoMethodError on nil when calling .scrub on i.content for RSS feeds lacking content in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `SimpleRSS` items may not have a `content` field (many feeds only provide `description`/`summary`), in which case `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no nil guard or fallback, so this is a real runtime defect for such feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) lacks timeout, size limit, and error handling in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:22

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after requiring `open-uri`. This performs an unbounded network fetch with no explicit open/read timeouts, no response size limits, and no rescue/handling for network/parse errors. As a scheduled job, this can hang workers or crash the job on transient failures or large responses, so the diff does introduce the stated robustness/security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, redirect/host check, size limit, or error handling in app/models/topic_embed.rb:51

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import_remote, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the new method starting at `def self.import_remote`). This uses open-uri to fetch remote content with no explicit open/read timeouts, no rescue/error handling around network failures, and no response size limiting before slurping the entire body into memory via `.read`. Also, while TopicRetriever.invalid_host? checks the *original* URL host, `open(url)` can follow HTTP redirects to a different host, so there is no post-redirect host validation here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via unescaped URL interpolation in app/models/topic_embed.rb:16

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing `url` directly into an `` tag: `"#{url}"` without any escaping/sanitization. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the `href` attribute (e.g. `http://good.com' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization) and later rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, this becomes a stored XSS vector in the imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF vulnerability via open() following redirects bypassing host equality check in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10-12

adjudication.rationale: The embed flow can fetch remote content via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) without restricting redirects. Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host` equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, that check only validates the *initial* URL’s host. If an attacker supplies an allowed-host URL that 30x redirects to an internal/metadata URL, open-uri will follow the redirect and perform the request anyway, enabling SSRF. The proposed finding mis-cites the controller lines (the `open()` call isn’t there), but the underlying redirect-bypass SSRF issue is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Job storm and duplicate topic creation race condition due to lack of deduplication before enqueuing RetrieveTopic jobs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` on every request, with no attempt to dedupe/lock at enqueue time. The `loading.html.erb` view auto-reloads every 30s, so a single embed page can enqueue repeated `retrieve_topic` jobs until the topic is created, and multiple simultaneous visitors can enqueue many more (a job storm). While `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles *execution* via Redis, it does not prevent the queue from filling with redundant jobs. Additionally, if throttling is bypassed (`no_throttle` for staff) two jobs can race past `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and attempt creation concurrently (unique index may prevent duplicates but can still cause failures).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous execution of Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside RetrieveTopic job causes unnecessary feed fetching and blocks workers

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and parses the entire feed (`rss.items.each`), which can be slow and will run inside the `RetrieveTopic` workflow (invoked from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), blocking that Sidekiq worker thread and potentially repeating a full feed fetch for each embed retrieval attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrescued TopicView.new causes 500 errors on embed endpoint for deleted or inaccessible topics in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:8

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, TopicView.new is only called when a topic_id is returned from TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url), i.e., when there is an existing TopicEmbed row. The diff does not show TopicView raising unhandled exceptions nor that such exceptions would result in a 500 (Rails/Discourse commonly rescue RecordNotFound/NotFound into 404). The claim about “deleted or inaccessible topics” causing 500s is speculative based on code not present in the diff and not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage uses full request.referer as targetOrigin, causing message delivery to fail if referer contains path/query or is blank in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that postMessage is using the full referrer URL as targetOrigin instead of just the origin (scheme+host+port), which can include path/query or be blank and thus cause the message to be dropped/fail, breaking resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak origin validation using substring check instead of exact match in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:21
ensure_embeddable requires request.referer, breaking embeds on scheme mismatch or when referer is stripped by browser privacy settings in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24-25

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable the code raises an InvalidAccess error unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. When `request.referer` is nil/blank (e.g., stripped by browser privacy settings), `URI('')` yields a nil host and the check fails, so embeds will be rejected. The “scheme mismatch” part isn’t supported by the diff because only the host is compared, not the scheme, but the hard dependency on Referer being present is real and verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 30s reload loop with no backoff or error handling causes infinite reloads if RetrieveTopic job fails in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the inline script unconditionally does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`. This view is rendered when `EmbedController#best` cannot find an existing `topic_id` and enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. If the `RetrieveTopic` job fails, is misconfigured (e.g., `embed_by_username` missing), or never creates a `TopicEmbed`, the controller will keep rendering `loading` and the page will reload every 30 seconds forever, with no retry limit/backoff or error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No locking around PollFeed allows concurrent pollers causing redundant work and race conditions in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:17

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Jobs::PollFeed` with no mutual exclusion/lock, and it can be executed concurrently from multiple places. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, meaning multiple simultaneous embed retrievals (and/or the hourly schedule) can trigger `poll_feed` at the same time. `poll_feed` then iterates items and calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which does a non-atomic `where(embed_url: url).first` check followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `embed_url`; concurrent pollers can race and one can raise on the unique constraint, causing redundant work and potential job failure. There is no locking/redis guard in `poll_feed.rb` to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls leaves protocol-relative URLs and relative URLs without leading slash untouched, producing broken links in app/models/topic_embed.rb:55-71

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten when the attribute starts_with?('/'). Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/x" *do* start with '/', so they will be rewritten (and mangled) into "#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x" — they are not left untouched as the finding claims. Separately, truly relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g., "images/x.png" or "../x") are left unchanged, which could cause broken links, but the proposed finding’s protocol-relative portion is a verifiable misread of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uri.port can be nil, causing malformed URLs with empty port colon in app/models/topic_embed.rb:65

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, `uri = URI(url)` is only called after `url` passes `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, ensuring an `http` or `https` URL. For `URI::HTTP`/`URI::HTTPS` objects, `uri.port` returns an integer default (80/443) when no explicit port is provided (it is not `nil`). Therefore the condition `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` will be false for normal URLs, and `prefix << ":#{uri.port}"` will not append an empty `:`. The proposed issue (nil port leading to a malformed `scheme://host:` prefix) is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:45-50 stubs TopicRetriever but the controller actually calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), so the test verifies a mock that doesn't match the real dispatch path

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best, when no topic_id is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders 'loading'; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever` directly. However spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (around the "tells the topic retriever to work" example) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, which will not be called by the controller. The controller only indirectly triggers TopicRetriever later via the RetrieveTopic job, so the spec’s mocked dispatch path does not match the actual code in this diff and would fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing spec/jobs/retrieve_topic_spec.rb; the job's logic including missing embed_url handling, user lookup, and no_throttle staff bypass is entirely untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` but does not add a corresponding spec file for it, while it does add specs for other new components (e.g., `poll_feed`, `topic_retriever`, `embed_controller`, `topic_embed`). However, “missing tests/untested logic” is a quality/coverage concern, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself. Nothing in the diff indicates that a `spec/jobs/retrieve_topic_spec.rb` is required for the build to pass or that the lack of it breaks functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:38-40 only tests guard conditions and mock delegation; the actual poll_feed body including open(), SimpleRSS.parse, URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, and TopicEmbed.import is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts that `execute` does/doesn’t call `poll_feed` based on settings (and mocks the delegation). There are no specs that execute `poll_feed` itself, so the newly added behavior in `poll_feed` (calling `open`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, iterating `rss.items`, URL fallback to `i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import`) is not exercised by tests introduced in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:31-44 stubs retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve, verifying method dispatch via mocks rather than real behavior like redis throttle, no_throttle bypass, and fetch_http fallback

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does stub `retrieved_recently?` and assert whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked, so it is testing dispatch rather than Redis throttling or the full retrieval path. However, this is a test-design/coverage critique, not a defect in the introduced production code. The diff does not show an incorrect throttle implementation; it only shows that the spec chooses to mock internal methods. That’s not a clear, verifiable bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote (readability fetch path) has no test, and absolutize_urls edge cases like protocol-relative URLs, absolute URLs, and non-default ports are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `open(url).read` + `Readability::Document`) but the added specs only cover `.import` and do not exercise `.import_remote` at all. Also, the `.import` spec only asserts relative-URL absolutization for href/src starting with `/` on a standard `http://host/path` URL, and does not cover protocol-relative URLs (`//...`), already-absolute URLs (`http(s)://...`), or the non-default-port branch in `absolutize_urls` (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`). These are verifiable test coverage gaps in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls port logic is buggy: it adds the port for any non-80/443 including when scheme is http on 443 or https on 80, and prepends ':'/'/' oddly

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the base prefix is built as `scheme://host` and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats both 80 and 443 as “default” for all schemes, which is incorrect: for `http` only 80 is default, and for `https` only 443 is default. As a result, URLs like `http://example.com:443/...` or `https://example.com:80/...` would incorrectly omit the explicit port when rewriting relative links/images. The claim about adding `:/` oddly is not supported (it appends `":#{uri.port}"` and then `"/"`, which is normal), but the port-defaulting logic issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers malformed referer URI in embed_controller_spec.rb; the rescue URI::InvalidURIError branch in ensure_embeddable is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` with a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch (triggered if `URI(request.referer || '')` raises). The new `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers missing `referer` and normal success paths, but does not include any case where `request.referer` is a malformed URI that would raise `URI::InvalidURIError`. Therefore, that rescue branch is not exercised by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No dedicated PostRevisor spec verifying that validations are actually skipped when @opts[:skip_validations] is passed to @post.save

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` to call `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, but it does not introduce (or remove) any spec for `PostRevisor`. The proposed finding is about test coverage (“no dedicated spec verifying ...”) rather than a bug/correctness/security defect in the code itself. While it’s true there isn’t a new spec explicitly asserting this behavior, missing a dedicated test is not a verifiable problem in the diff (the behavior implemented is straightforward and used elsewhere via `skip_validations: true`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:51-53 stubs TopicView.expects(:new) but never verifies the best template renders, discourse_expires_in is set, or @topic_view is assigned for the view

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` are test assertions about the controller behavior (that `TopicView.new` is called with certain args). The proposed finding is essentially asking for additional test coverage (verifying template rendering, `discourse_expires_in`, or instance variable assignment), but the diff does not show a defect in the production code caused by this. Not asserting those extra details is not a verifiable bug/correctness/security issue introduced by the diff; it’s a test completeness preference. Also, the controller does set `@topic_view` when `topic_id` is present and calls `discourse_expires_in` regardless, so there’s no clear failing behavior demonstrated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb view logic is fragile/coupled to controller internals: @topic_view could be nil when accessed in the else branch (embed.start_discussion), relying on controller behavior to guarantee safety

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, @topic_view is only needed when rendering the `best` template: when `topic_id` is present it is always assigned (`@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`). When `topic_id` is nil, the controller does not render `best` at all; it enqueues a job and explicitly `render 'loading'`. Therefore, under the control flow shown in the diff, `best.html.erb` will not execute with a nil `@topic_view`, so the alleged nil access in the else branch is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:13 mutates the contents string argument with <<, which raises or corrupts if the caller passes a frozen or shared string; should use a new string or dup

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the method does `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the caller-provided `contents` string in place. This is verifiable in the diff. In Ruby, `<<` will raise `FrozenError` if the passed string is frozen and can also create unintended side effects if the caller reuses the same string instance elsewhere (it will now have the footer appended). Nothing in the method contract indicates it intends to mutate its argument, and it could safely use `contents = contents.dup` or string concatenation to avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:41 uses Kernel#open on an arbitrary URL (SSRF risk, unsafe, file handle never closed); same pattern in poll_feed.rb with open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is SSRF via PollFeed calling open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL. The candidate explicitly flags Kernel#open on arbitrary URLs as an SSRF risk and notes the same pattern in poll_feed.rb with open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url), which matches the underlying concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:7 import method does too much (creates topic/post/embed, updates posts, appends footer HTML, absolutizes URLs) — separation-of-concerns issue and duplication risk with import_remote

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import` indeed performs multiple responsibilities (mutating `contents`, creating/updating `Post`/`TopicEmbed`, and calling `absolutize_urls`), and `import_remote` delegates to `import`. However, this is a design/maintainability critique (separation of concerns / potential duplication) rather than a concrete, verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness) introduced by the change. The code as shown is internally consistent (e.g., `import_remote` ultimately reuses `import`), so the finding is not a clear problem in the diff under the stated criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:40 directly invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) from within perform_retrieve, coupling TopicRetriever to Jobs::PollFeed, bypassing Sidekiq scheduling, and re-fetching the entire RSS feed rather than the requested URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true, it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly. That is a synchronous invocation of the scheduled job class, bypassing the normal Sidekiq scheduling/queueing semantics for that job. Also, Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed unconditionally fetches and iterates the entire configured feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url); rss.items.each`), importing every item, not just the specific `@embed_url` being retrieved. So a request to retrieve a single embed URL can trigger a full feed refetch and bulk imports, which is a verifiable coupling/behavioral defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:31 assumes i.content is always present; SimpleRSS items may not have content for all feeds (e.g., RSS 2.0 without content:encoded), raising NoMethodError on nil

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for many RSS feeds that only provide `description`/`summary` and no `content:encoded`), `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no nil-guard or fallback to another field in the diff, so this is a real correctness bug introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 / topic_embed.rb / best.html.erb: imported RSS HTML is stored uncooked (cook_method: :raw_html) and rendered via raw post.cooked with no sanitization, creating an XSS vector if the feed is untrusted

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: Post#cook now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`. TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (with `skip_validations: true`). In Jobs::PollFeed, `contents` comes from `i.content` (RSS/Atom) and is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`—no sanitization/whitelisting is applied before storing. The embed view then outputs it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for these posts equals the original HTML. This combination creates a straightforward XSS vector if the feed/content source is untrusted or compromised (e.g., script tags, event handlers, or `javascript:` URLs in allowed attributes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.rb:132 returning raw for cook_method == raw_html skips the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) pipeline entirely for raw_html posts, causing hidden behavior difference for plugins relying on that filter

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. That early return happens before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so the `:after_post_cook` hook is not executed for raw_html posts. This is a concrete behavioral change introduced by the diff and can break plugins that rely on that filter to post-process cooked content, even if skipping the normal cooking pipeline is intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:11 TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) is called without verifying the topic still exists; a deleted topic or stale embed topic_id will raise inside TopicView

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code does assume that a non-nil `topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` corresponds to an existing topic and does not explicitly re-check existence before calling `TopicView.new(...)`. However, the proposed finding’s key claim (“will raise inside TopicView”) is not verifiable from this diff: `TopicView` implementation and Discourse/Rails exception handling (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` mapping to 404) are outside the diff, and there is no direct evidence here that a stale `topic_id` can occur (cleanup on topic deletion may exist elsewhere). As written, this is an edge-case speculation rather than a clear defect demonstrated by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:24 URI(request.referer || '') with empty string returns a URI with host=nil; behavior is fragile and coupled to URI parsing quirks across Ruby versions

adjudication.rationale: In `ensure_embeddable`, `URI(request.referer || '').host` being `nil` when the referer is missing is intentional: it causes the subsequent comparison to fail and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (“invalid referer host”). This behavior is covered by the controller spec (“raises an error with no referer”). Even if `URI('')` behavior differed, the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` path still raises the same access error, so there’s no clear defect introduced by this diff—only speculative concern about Ruby version quirks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: layouts/embed.html.erb:9 parent.postMessage with request.referer interpolated raw into JS is an XSS vector if referer contains quotes/newlines, and postMessage throws if referer is empty/invalid
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `request.referer` is interpolated raw into JavaScript in `layouts/embed.html.erb`, creating an XSS vector if the referer contains malicious characters. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (unescaped header injected into JS leading to XSS), though it also mentions an extra potential runtime error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: layouts/embed.html.erb:10 document['body'].offsetHeight uses bracket notation instead of document.body, which may behave unexpectedly in strict mode or some browsers

adjudication.rationale: In layouts/embed.html.erb, `document['body']` is simply bracket-notation access to the standard `document.body` property. This is valid JavaScript and is not affected by strict mode (strict mode restricts certain syntax/assignments, not property access style). Since it runs inside `window.onload`, `document.body` (and thus `document['body']`) will be available. The finding is therefore a style nit rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:11 discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is a substring match that a malicious origin like http://notdiscourse.com.evildomain.com could pass; should compare parsed origins exactly
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: using indexOf/substring matching for origin validation is bypassable by crafted malicious domains that include the trusted domain as a substring; the candidate even gives an example and suggests exact parsed-origin comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:53 absolutize_urls only handles /-prefixed hrefs, not protocol-relative //host URLs or relative URLs without leading slash, leaving broken links in imported content

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href`/`src` is present and `start_with?('/')`. Any other relative forms (e.g. `href="post.html"`, `href="../post"`, `src="images/a.png"`) are left unchanged, despite the method’s stated goal (“Convert any relative URLs to absolute”). Those unchanged relative URLs would then resolve relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source site, producing broken links in imported content. (Protocol-relative `//host/...` isn’t rewritten either, but that form typically still works; the unhandled non-slash-relative paths are the clear defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: migration 20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 sets default: 1 but Post.cook_maps :regular to 0 and :raw_html to 1, so existing posts get raw_html cook method, rendering their raw content uncooked — critical data corruption/breakage for all existing posts

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `posts.cook_method` with `default: 1`. In this codebase, the custom `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` pattern (also used for `Post.types`) is typically 1-based (e.g., existing Discourse `post_type` uses 1 for `:regular`). Nothing in the diff shows `Enum` is 0-based, and the finding’s claim that `:regular` maps to 0 / `:raw_html` to 1 is not verifiable from the diff and is likely incorrect. With 1-based enums, default 1 correctly corresponds to `:regular`, so existing posts would continue to be cooked normally, not treated as `raw_html`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:21 if TopicEmbed.create! raises inside the transaction, the post rolls back but the post variable remains set to the stale rolled-back record and is returned to callers

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `TopicEmbed.create!` call is inside a `Topic.transaction` block. If `create!` raises, Rails will roll back the transaction and re-raise the exception (there is no rescue in this method). Therefore the method will not continue to the final `post` return and will not return a “stale rolled-back record” to callers; it will error out instead. The described behavior (returning a stale `post` after rollback) is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:46 and poll_feed.rb:25 duplicate User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase) lookup; should be a shared helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain two similar lookups (Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed and TopicRetriever#fetch_http both do `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`). However, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change—it's a refactoring suggestion to DRY code. The duplication does not change behavior or introduce an error on its own, so it doesn't qualify as a "real problem" under the instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing migration 'create_top_topics' modified to add 'force: true', which will DROP TABLE and destroy data if the migration has already been applied in any environment

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an old migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop an existing `top_topics` table *if the migration’s `up` were executed when the table already exists*, Rails will not re-run an already-applied migration (it is tracked in `schema_migrations`). So in a normal deploy where the migration has already been applied, this code path won’t execute and won’t drop data. Also, even without `force: true`, rolling back/redoing this migration would drop the table anyway (Rails reverses `create_table` with `drop_table`). Therefore the finding’s claim that this change will drop the table “if the migration has already been applied” is not a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New migration 'create_topic_embeds' uses 'force: true' on a brand-new table, which can drop the table and any data if it already exists from a prior failed run

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the migration calls `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists before recreating it. Even though this is a new migration, if the table exists due to a prior partial/failed migration run or manual creation, rerunning this migration would drop it and any data in it. The risk is directly implied by the `force: true` option present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NOT NULL columns 'topic_id' and 'post_id' on 'topic_embeds' table lack corresponding model-level validations, causing DB constraint violations instead of clean validation errors

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `topic_id` and `post_id` as `null: false`, but the `TopicEmbed` model only validates presence of `embed_url` and `content_sha1` (it has `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` but no `validates_presence_of :topic_id, :post_id`). In Rails versions where `belongs_to` does not enforce presence by default, attempting to create/save a `TopicEmbed` without those IDs would bypass model validation and fail at the DB layer with a NOT NULL violation rather than a clean validation error. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default value of 1 for 'cook_method' column relies on Discourse's Enum starting at ordinal 1, making it fragile and potentially causing raw HTML rendering if the Enum implementation changes

adjudication.rationale: The migration sets `posts.cook_method` default to `1` and the model defines `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. This matches the established pattern already in `Post.types` (also using `Enum.new(...)` and implicitly relying on the same ordinal mapping). There is no verifiable defect in the diff showing that `Enum` is 0-based or unstable; the finding hinges on hypothetical future changes to `Enum` rather than a concrete problem introduced here. If `Enum` semantics changed, it would break existing enums too, not uniquely this column default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS vulnerability via raw-HTML cook method and `raw` rendering of external content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` mode, and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when that mode is set, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where sanitization would typically happen). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts for external content (RSS/Atom/remote pages) using `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and it passes `contents` (from `SimpleRSS.parse(open(...))` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, or from `Readability::Document#content`) directly into `raw` after only URL absolutization—no sanitization is performed. The embed view then renders this HTML with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. As a result, untrusted external HTML can be stored and later rendered as HTML, enabling stored XSS (e.g., malicious feed content containing `<script>` or event handlers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: URL injection / attribute breakout in the import footer due to insufficient URL validation

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `TopicEmbed.import` appends an HTML footer containing `#{url}` without any escaping, and the only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. That regex allows quotes and other characters after the scheme (e.g. `http://example.com/' onmouseover='...`), which can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML. Since these imported posts are stored with `cook_method :raw_html` and later rendered via `raw post.cooked`, the injected HTML would be emitted to clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on items without `content`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS/Atom item lacks a `content` field (common; many feeds use `description`/`summary` instead), `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`. There is no nil-guard or fallback, so the job can crash on such items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to an already-shipped migration could drop existing tables and data

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) by changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. Because this is a previously-created migration (not a new one), altering it means that if this migration is ever executed again in an environment where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., rollback/re-run, inconsistent DB state, or manual table creation), it can drop existing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF vulnerability via retriever because the referer check is not a real boundary
Weak postMessage origin check using substring `indexOf` instead of origin equality

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring check, not an origin equality check. As a result, an origin can be accepted if it merely appears anywhere inside `discourseUrl` (e.g., `discourseUrl = "https://evil.example/?o=https://discourse.example"` would allow messages from `https://discourse.example`). A strict comparison against the expected origin derived from `discourseUrl` (scheme+host+port) would be required to reliably ensure messages only come from the intended Discourse instance. Therefore the finding identifies a real, verifiable weakness in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `skip_validations` disables ActiveRecord validations on revises for externally sourced content

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces support for skipping ActiveRecord validations during revisions: `PostRevisor#update_post` changes from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` for imported/embedded content. This does mean validations are bypassed for externally sourced updates, but it is an explicit, deliberate behavior added in the diff (and imports already pass `skip_validations: true` on creation via `PostCreator`). As written, this is not a clear bug/defect by itself; it’s a design decision unless specific harmful validations being bypassed are identified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: User request triggers a full synchronous PollFeed run causing potential denial-of-service

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued), and `PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a full remote fetch/parse of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` via `open(...)` and iterates all `rss.items`. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, so a user-triggered request can cause this full feed poll to run synchronously inside the Sidekiq job. The only throttle is per-embed-url (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying `embed_url` can still repeatedly trigger expensive feed polling, creating a plausible DoS vector against job workers when feed polling is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open()` used on URLs poses a command-injection risk if a pipe is passed
Disqus importer silently regressed due to removed `--category` option and switching to `import_remote`

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all logic that looked up `Category` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The importer now creates the topic via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` never sets a category, so imports can no longer be directed to a specified category. This is a concrete behavior regression introduced by the diff (and it’s “silent” because the option is simply gone, with no replacement).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Infinite reload loop on retrieval failure in the embed loading view

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the script unconditionally runs `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`. In `EmbedController#best`, this loading view is rendered whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil. If the background retrieval (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`) fails, is misconfigured (e.g., `embed_by_username` missing), or can never produce a `TopicEmbed` for that URL, the controller will keep rendering `loading` and the page will reload every 30 seconds indefinitely with no retry limit or error state. This is a real, directly verifiable infinite reload loop under retrieval failure conditions introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `content_sha1` computed on pre-absolutized content can leave stale relative-URL rendering

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` before `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` is applied, but `absolutize_urls` is a deterministic transformation of the same `contents` using the (unchanged) `embed_url` as the base. Since updates are keyed by the same `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)`), the base URL used for absolutization does not change for an existing record. Therefore, if `contents` hasn’t changed, the absolutized rendering also won’t change, so computing the SHA1 pre-absolutization does not cause “stale relative-URL rendering” in a verifiable way from this diff.
